answer: Cross-Epoch Divergence Catch. Each identity must harbor a public thread of per-epoch action vectors; the protocol compares consecutive epochs and flags any identity whose distribution diverges beyond a set threshold. A plume of correlated anomalies across epochs marks the identity as sybil. Attackers must maintain consistent behaviour across every epoch, raising the cost of running many identities: each one needs sustained, non-divergent activity, so scaling up multiplies the operational work and detection risk per identity.
